scenarios.title: Lost webhook on a slot: the sweep reconciles against Stripe — confirms the paid order, keeps the seat

checks.description: slot/book accepted and returned a Checkout url
a holding order exists after booking
the seat was claimed (seats_taken = 1)
the guest was charged (PaymentIntent succeeded)
the mis-signed webhook was rejected (400), so nothing confirmed it
the order is still holding (the webhook never landed)
the sweep ran
the sweep reported a reconciliation
STRIPE: the charge is captured (money really moved)
STRIPE: the provider was paid — £6 fee to us, £54 transferred to them
STRIPE: the provider’s connected balance rose by ~£54 net
APP: the order was RECONCILED to confirmed (not expired)
APP: the order now carries the PaymentIntent id
APP: the seat was KEPT (seats_taken still 1 — not resold)

scenarios.note: FIXED: the paid order was reconciled to confirmed and the seat kept — the charge is no longer orphaned.

scenarios.title: Card declined halfway (request shape): no order stranded, nothing held

checks.description: STRIPE: the charge was declined
STRIPE: code is card_declined

scenarios.note: Slot shape differs: the seat is claimed before the card, so a decline there parks the seat until the sweep (~35 min). Nothing is charged either way.

scenarios.title: Provider never responds: the 48h hold is released by the sweep, nothing captured

checks.description: an authorised order exists
the sweep ran
STRIPE: the hold was cancelled, nothing captured
APP: the order is expired

scenarios.note: The sweep sends the guest no email on expiry (the decline path does) — a notification gap, not a money error.

scenarios.title: Cancel after payment, inside the window: provider keeps 90%, platform keeps its 10%, no refund

checks.description: the order is confirmed and captured
cancel (forfeit) succeeded with no refund
STRIPE: nothing was refunded (money stays put)
STRIPE: our £18 application fee was NOT refunded
APP: the order is cancelled and records the forfeit (cancel_ack)

scenarios.note: Provider keeps 90% and the platform keeps its 10% on an experience that will not happen — a policy choice for the solicitor.

scenarios.title: Refund issued: full refund to the guest, our 10% returned, the transfer reversed

checks.description: the order is confirmed and captured
orders/respond refund succeeded
STRIPE: the guest was refunded in full (£180)
STRIPE: our application fee was refunded — commission UNWOUND
STRIPE: the transfer to the provider was fully reversed
APP: the order is refunded

scenarios.note: No partial-refund path exists for experiences, so the cottage "partial refund keeps the fee" bug has no analogue here.

scenarios.title: Lost webhook on a request (chef): the sweep reconciles against Stripe — rebuilds the authorised order, hold kept

checks.description: the card is HELD not charged (requires_capture)
the mis-signed webhook was rejected (400)
APP: no order row exists yet (the webhook never landed)
the sweep ran
the sweep reported a rebuild
APP: an order row now exists (rebuilt from Stripe)
APP: it is authorised, awaiting the provider
APP: it carries the held PaymentIntent
APP: it belongs to the right guest and provider

STRIPE: the hold was captured on confirm (£180)

scenarios.title: Add guests: child-order top-up — race, abandon+sweep, cancel refunds both PIs + both seats, invite cap rises

checks.description: A: booked 5 of 6 places
A: the parent is confirmed
A: exactly one top-up won the last seat
A: the session is full (seats_taken = 6), never oversold
B: booked 1 place
B: top-up accepted (holding child + Checkout)
B: a holding child order exists
B: the added seat was claimed (seats_taken = 2)
B: the sweep ran
B: the abandoned child is EXPIRED
B: the added seat was released (back to 1)
C: booked 2 places
C: the parent is confirmed
D: invite cap is 1 before the top-up (2 seats − the booker)
D: ensure_order_seats minted 1 seat row for the 2-seat order
C: top-up accepted
C: the top-up child is confirmed
C: the parent total was NOT rewritten (still £40)
D: invite cap rose to 2 after the top-up confirmed
D: ensure_order_seats minted a 2nd seat row once the top-up confirmed (family = 3 − booker)
C: the session holds all 3 seats
C: cancel refunded (free window)
C: STRIPE — the original £40 was refunded and its transfer reversed
C: STRIPE — the added £20 refunded SEPARATELY and its transfer reversed
C: APP — both orders are refunded
C: BOTH seat claims were released (seats_taken back to 0)

scenarios.note: Add-guests reuses the slot machine: child order per added place, its own PI and seats, confirmed by the same webhook, swept if unpaid; a full cancel settles the whole family.

scenarios.title: Move a booking: the whole family (parent + top-up) moves together, or nobody does; a full target and a past-cutoff target are both refused

checks.description: A: paid family of 3 built (parent 2 + top-up 1)
A: the source holds all 3 seats before the move
A: move succeeded
A: the WHOLE family moved (2 rows, 3 seats)
A: the move names BOTH times (old → new)
A: parent repointed to the new session, re-dated, and stamped
A: the top-up child rode along (same new session, stamped)
A: the source released all 3 seats
A: the target claimed all 3 seats
B: paid family of 3 built on a second session
B: the move was REFUSED (no room for the whole family)
B: the family did NOT move (still on the source, never stamped)
B: the source is untouched (still 3 seats)
B: the full target is untouched (still 4 seats)
C: a move into a slot past its own cutoff is REFUSED
C: the family still did NOT move
C: the past-cutoff target claimed nobody

scenarios.note: The move is one atomic RPC: it locks the family and both sessions, re-checks capacity and the cutoff under lock, then claims the target and releases the source — or raises and rolls the whole thing back, leaving the source exactly as it was.

scenarios.title: Change count down: a reduction refunds the difference at once and lowers the payout

checks.description: a confirmed per-person order, £165 for 3
change-count down is accepted
STRIPE — £55 was refunded to the card
price stays £165 (the original charge); £55 is recorded as refunded, count now 2

scenarios.note: Payout follows automatically: orderNet = (price − amount_refunded) × (1 − rate) = (165 − 55) × 0.9 = £99, down from £148.50.

the order records £300 for a party of 6 (220 + 2×£40)
a party of 9 is REFUSED — over the stay of 8 / the item max

scenarios.title: An increase holds the extra on the card; the provider accepts and it is captured

checks.description: the increase is a REQUEST — a Checkout hold, not an instant charge
a holding child was written for the extra place (£55)
the completed hold is now AUTHORISED — a request to answer
accept succeeds
STRIPE — the £55 hold was CAPTURED on accept

scenarios.note: The accepted extra is its own destination charge, so the provider payout is the sum across the order family.

scenarios.title: Past the window every change is closed; inside it a date change is a provider request

checks.description: change-count is CLOSED past the window (409)
change-date is CLOSED past the window (409)
a date change is a REQUEST, not an instant move
the requested date is parked and the order stays on its date
the provider accepts the date and it applies
the booking is now on the new date, the request cleared

scenarios.title: The provider’s payout follows every change

checks.description: after a reduce, the payable net drops (orderNet = (price − refunded) × 0.9)

scenarios.note: There is no payout cron for experiences — the provider is paid by the destination charge, netting off amount_refunded; a reduce reverses the transfer, an accepted increase adds its own charge.
